description: Ground-truth questions for retrieval, version comparison, contradiction detection, risk assessment, citations, and insufficient-evidence behavior over the bundled policy pairs.

questions.question: What is the new minimum attendance requirement and what did it replace?
questions.expectedAnswer: The new policy requires 80% attendance in each course, replacing 75% in each course.

questions.question: How did medical attendance condonation change?
questions.expectedAnswer: The maximum shortage fell from 10 percentage points to five, the filing deadline changed from seven calendar days to three business days after return, and decisions moved from the Head of Department to the Medical and Accessibility Review Panel.
expectedFacts: seven calendar days to three business days

questions.question: What attendance level does the new policy require for laboratory and clinical courses?
questions.expectedAnswer: The new attendance policy requires 85% for laboratory and clinical courses unless a statutory council requires more.

questions.question: Which units gained new responsibilities under the attendance revision?
questions.expectedAnswer: Academic Affairs operates monitoring, academic advisors document intervention, and the Medical and Accessibility Review Panel decides exemptions; Heads of Department retain data-certification but lose condonation authority.

questions.question: How quickly must marks be submitted under the new examination policy?
questions.expectedAnswer: The academic department must submit an approved mark sheet within five calendar days after the examination, replacing the old ten-calendar-day examiner deadline.

questions.question: What changed for question-paper submission?
questions.expectedAnswer: The old sealed-paper deadline was ten business days before the exam. The new department coordinator must upload a moderated paper through the secure portal fifteen calendar days before the exam, and the department now removes metadata and confirms accessibility.
expectedFacts: ten business days to fifteen calendar days

questions.question: How long are examination records retained under the new policy?
questions.expectedAnswer: Answer scripts, moderation records, and final mark sheets are retained for seven years after result publication, replacing five-year retention.

questions.question: May students use generative AI in a graded assignment under the new student AI policy?
questions.expectedAnswer: Yes, but only when the assessment brief expressly labels AI-assisted use as permitted and defines allowed functions; silence means prohibited, and exams, viva responses, and independent-work tasks remain prohibited.

questions.question: What disclosure is required when student AI use is permitted?
questions.expectedAnswer: The student must name the tool, date, purpose, and material influence, retain material prompts and outputs through the appeal period, and provide them on request.

questions.question: Do the new student AI and faculty responsibility policies agree about AI-assisted graded work?
questions.expectedAnswer: No. The student AI policy conditionally permits AI-assisted graded work when a brief authorizes it, while the faculty policy requires every graded assignment to prohibit AI-generated content and says faculty may not authorize it.

questions.question: What student-record retention period changed in the privacy policy?
questions.expectedAnswer: The old general rule retained student records for five years after leaving. The new schedule retains routine student-service records, advising notes, attendance source logs, and unsuccessful applications for three years after the last active relationship, with separate permanent and seven-year categories.
expectedFacts: five years to three years for routine records

questions.question: What is the new deadline for reporting a suspected data incident?
questions.expectedAnswer: It must be reported to the service desk and Data Protection Office within 24 hours of discovery; the old policy used an as-soon-as-practicable report and a 72-hour senior-management escalation for material harm.

questions.question: What must each department do under the new privacy policy?
questions.expectedAnswer: Each department head must appoint a data steward. The steward maintains a processing inventory, reviews access quarterly, coordinates deletion, and returns search results for rights requests within seven business days.

questions.question: How did the baseline placement CGPA requirement change?
questions.expectedAnswer: It rose from 6.5 to 7.0 on a ten-point scale.

questions.question: Did the backlog rule become stricter or more permissive in the new placement policy?
questions.expectedAnswer: It became more permissive at the college baseline: the old rule required no active backlog, while the new rule allows one, though an employer may prohibit active backlogs.

questions.question: Is the placement attendance requirement consistent with the new general attendance policy?
questions.expectedAnswer: No. The new placement policy still certifies 75% in each current course, while the new attendance policy requires 80% generally and 85% for laboratory or clinical courses.

questions.question: When must faculty publish course and assessment information under the new responsibilities policy?
questions.expectedAnswer: Within five business days after classes begin, replacing ten business days.

questions.question: How did the coursework feedback deadline change for faculty?
questions.expectedAnswer: It shortened from 15 business days to 10 business days, with a recorded cohort-wide extension available in the new policy.

questions.question: How do the new faculty and examination mark deadlines fit together?
questions.expectedAnswer: Faculty submit verified marks to the department coordinator within four calendar days, allowing the department to validate and meet the examination policy's five-calendar-day institutional deadline.

questions.question: Which bundled policy conflicts should be treated as critical before the 2026 policies take effect?
questions.expectedAnswer: At minimum, reviewers should resolve the direct AI-permission conflict between the student and faculty policies and the 75% placement-attendance rule against the 80%/85% general attendance rule.
expectedFacts: student AI versus faculty AI conflict

questions.question: What is the college cafeteria's refund policy for unused meal credits?
questions.expectedAnswer: I could not find sufficient evidence in the uploaded policies.

questions.question: Who may reopen a locked mark sheet under the old and new examination policies?
questions.expectedAnswer: The old policy allowed only the Controller of Examinations. The new policy requires two-person approval by the Head of Department and Controller.

questions.question: What should the Examination Office change before implementing the new policies?
questions.expectedAnswer: It should consume the centrally locked eligibility list, operate the secure question-paper portal and second mark validation, support standing accessibility arrangements, adopt the two-person reopening control, and retain examination records for seven years with Records Office disposal approval.

questions.question: Are the new privacy and examination policies aligned on examination-record retention?
questions.expectedAnswer: Yes. Both require a seven-year period after results are published for answer scripts or examination records, and both recognize holds that suspend destruction.
